l: prosperity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 1
s: Because of the church’s steadiness, its members become exceedingly rich and have abundance of flocks, herds, grain, precious metals, silk, linen, and cloth. They use their prosperous circumstances to provide for those in need.

l: pride, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 1
s: Nehor is lifted up in the pride of his heart and wears costly apparel. Many among the church also become proud and contend warmly with their adversaries, even using their fists.

l: riches, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 1
s: Nehor receives money from those who believe his words and preaches false doctrines for riches and honor. The church members become rich but do not set their hearts upon riches and are liberal to those in need.

l: swords, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 1
s: Nehor draws his sword and strikes Gideon, killing him. Nehor’s attempt to enforce priestcraft by the sword is condemned by Alma.

l: labor, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 1
s: Nehor teaches that priests and teachers should not labor with their hands but should be supported by the people. In the church, priests and hearers return diligently to their labors, and everyone labors according to strength.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: Amlici draws many people after him and seeks to become king, but the voice of the people rejects him, so his followers consecrate him as king and become Amlicites. Amlici commands his people to fight the Nephites, leading to war at the hill Amnihu and later across the river Sidon. Alma leads the Nephites, kills Amlici, and helps defeat the Amlicites and Lamanites. The Nephites pursue their enemies into the wilderness, where many die from wounds and are devoured by beasts and vultures.

l: Amlici, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: Amlici is described as a cunning and worldly-wise man who draws many people after him and seeks to become king. After the voice of the people rejects him, his followers consecrate him as king; he commands them to fight the Nephites, and Alma kills him with the sword.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: Alma is the chief judge and governor of the people of Nephi. He leads the Nephites in battle, prays for his life to be spared so he can preserve his people, kills Amlici, and defeats the guards of the king of the Lamanites.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The people assemble throughout the land to decide whether Amlici should become king. They divide according to their views, and the voice of the people comes against Amlici.

l: church of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The church of God is threatened by Amlici because he intends to destroy it. The people of the church are alarmed that Amlici might gain authority over them.

l: Amlicites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The Amlicites are Amlici's followers and are distinguished by his name. They fight the Nephites, join the Lamanites, and are defeated and pursued into the wilderness.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites are the remainder of the people who do not follow Amlici and are called the people of God. They arm themselves, fight the Amlicites and Lamanites, and defeat them with the strength of the Lord.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The Lamanites join the Amlicites and attack the people near the land of Zarahemla. They are defeated by the Nephites and flee into the wilderness.

l: contention, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: Contention begins among the people in the commencement of the fifth year of their reign because of Amlici's effort to become king. The people gather in separate bodies with much dispute and wonderful contentions.

l: establishing Amlici as king, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: Amlici's followers endeavor to establish him as king, but the voice of the people rejects him. His followers then gather together and consecrate him as their king.

l: voice of the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The voice of the people is required by law to establish such matters. It comes against Amlici, so he is not made king over the people by that voice.

l: war between the Nephites and Amlicites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The war begins after Amlici commands his people to take up arms against the Nephites. The Nephites defeat the Amlicites, though many people on both sides are slain.

l: battle at the hill Amnihu, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The Amlicites come upon the hill Amnihu and begin making war with the Nephites. Alma leads the Nephites, who eventually defeat the Amlicites there.

l: crossing of the river Sidon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites cross the river Sidon while the Lamanites and Amlicites attack them. Alma clears the west bank by throwing slain Lamanites into the river so his people can cross and continue fighting.

l: law of Mosiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The law requires matters such as establishing a king to be decided by the voice of the people.

l: rights and privileges, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The people fear that if Amlici gains the voice of the people, he will deprive them of the rights and privileges of the church.

l: hill Amnihu, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The hill Amnihu is east of the river Sidon. The Amlicites attack the Nephites there, and many Nephites fall before the Lord strengthens them.

l: river Sidon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The river Sidon runs by the land of Zarahemla. The Nephites cross it during the battle, and the bodies of slain Lamanites are thrown into its waters to clear a passage.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The river Sidon runs by the land of Zarahemla. The Lamanites and Amlicites attack the Nephites near this land.

l: city of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The city of Zarahemla is the city toward which the Nephites depart from the valley of Gideon. The spies warn that the Lamanites and Amlicites may obtain possession of it.

l: the valley of Gideon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 2
s: The valley of Gideon is named after Gideon, who was slain by Nehor with the sword. After pursuing the Amlicites, Alma causes the Nephites to pitch their tents there for the night.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites bury their dead after battles with the Lamanites and Amlicites, then return to their lands and establish peace after driving out another Lamanite army. The Lamanites and Amlicites are described by their markings, appearance, traditions, rebellion, and warfare against the Nephites. The Lord God’s promises concerning the curse and mark are fulfilled as the Amlicites mark themselves and bring the curse upon themselves. The wars and contentions in the fifth year of the reign of the judges result in thousands and tens of thousands dying according to the spirit they obeyed.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The Nephites bury those slain in battle and return to their lands, houses, wives, and children. They send an army that drives the remaining Lamanites out of their borders and then establish peace. Those who believe the records from the land of Jerusalem, follow correct traditions, and keep the commandments of God are called Nephites.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites kill Nephites, including women and children, and destroy flocks, herds, and fields. Their heads are shorn, and they wear limited clothing and armor while using bows, arrows, stones, and slings. Their skins are dark according to the mark set upon their fathers, and another Lamanite army is driven out of the Nephite lands.

l: Amlicites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The Amlicites fight the Nephites alongside the Lamanites and are slain in large numbers. They distinguish themselves by marking their foreheads red, without shorning their heads like the Lamanites. They come out in open rebellion against God and bring the curse upon themselves.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The Lord God sets a mark upon Laman, Lemuel, the sons of Ishmael, and Ishmaelitish women so their seed may be distinguished from the seed of their brethren. He promises blessings to Nephi and his seed and declares that those who fight against or depart from them will receive a mark or no longer be called their seed.

l: battle between the Lamanites and Amlicites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The battle is fought in the land of Zarahemla in the fifth year of the reign of the judges. Many Lamanites and Amlicites are slain, and the slain Lamanites and Amlicites are cast into the waters of the river Sidon.

l: war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The wars and contentions in the fifth year of the reign of the judges include the battle between the Lamanites and Amlicites and the later Lamanite attack. Thousands and tens of thousands die and are sent to the eternal world to reap rewards according to their works and the spirit they obeyed.

l: second Lamanite invasion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: Another Lamanite army comes into the Nephite lands not many days after the battle in the land of Zarahemla. Alma sends a numerous army against it, and the Nephites slay many Lamanites and drive the remainder out of their borders.

l: curse of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The curse is connected to the transgression and rebellion of Laman, Lemuel, the sons of Ishmael, and Ishmaelitish women. Those who mingle their seed with the Lamanites or are led away by the Lamanites receive the same curse, while the Amlicites bring the curse upon themselves through open rebellion.

l: mark, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The Lord God sets a mark upon the Lamanites and on those who mingle their seed with them, fight against Nephi and his seed, or depart from Nephi. The Amlicites set a red mark upon their own foreheads, fulfilling the word of God.

l: records, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The records brought out of the land of Jerusalem are believed by those called Nephites. The Nephites keep records that are true of their people and of the Lamanites.

l: the tradition of the Lamanites' fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites follow traditions that are described as incorrect and that would prove destructive. Those who believe the correct traditions of their fathers, together with the commandments of God, are called Nephites.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 3
s: The word of God concerning the Lamanites, the mark, the curse, those who mingle their seed, those who fight against Nephi’s seed, and those who depart from Nephi is fulfilled. The Amlicites unknowingly fulfill it when they mark themselves in their foreheads.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: In the sixth year of the reign of the judges, the people of Nephi suffered losses from the Lamanites and were awakened to their duty, leading to renewed establishment of the church of God and many baptisms. In the eighth year, the church became proud and contentious, persecuting others and setting a harmful example that caused the church to fail in its progress. Alma saw inequality, afflictions, and persecution among the people, while humble followers succored the poor and endured afflictions for Christ’s sake. At the commencement of the ninth year, Alma appointed Nephihah chief judge, relinquished the judgment-seat, retained the high priesthood, and devoted himself to preaching the word of God and bearing pure testimony.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma was consecrated high priest over the people of the church by the hand of his father Alma. He saw the church’s wickedness, inequality, and persecution, became sorrowful, and selected Nephihah as chief judge while retaining the office of high priest.

l: Nephihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Nephihah was a wise man among the elders of the church. Alma gave him power according to the voice of the people, and he was appointed chief judge to sit in the judgment-seat and govern the people.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: The people of Nephi suffered the loss of brethren, flocks, herds, and grain through the actions of the Lamanites. They experienced peace in the seventh year, but later some became proud, contentious, unequal, and persecuting, while others succored the poor and needy.

l: church of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: The church of God was established more fully, and about three thousand five hundred souls joined and were baptized in the seventh year. In the eighth year, many church members became proud, contentious, and persecuting, causing the church to fail in its progress.

l: judgment-seat, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma delivered the judgment-seat to Nephihah at the commencement of the ninth year. Nephihah used it to judge and govern the people.

l: high priesthood of the holy order of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma retained the high priesthood of the holy order of God after delivering the judgment-seat to Nephihah. He confined himself wholly to the high priesthood, the testimony of the word, and the spirit of revelation and prophecy.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma intended to preach the word of God among the people of Nephi to stir them up in remembrance of their duty. He believed the word of God could pull down pride, craftiness, and contentions and reclaim the people through pure testimony.

l: afflictions of the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: The people were greatly afflicted by the loss of their brethren, livestock, and grain. Alma also saw the afflictions of humble followers of God, including those who suffered for Christ’s sake.

l: baptism, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Many people were baptized in the waters of Sidon by Alma and joined the church of God. About three thousand five hundred souls were baptized in the seventh year.

l: church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: The people began to establish the church more fully after being awakened to a remembrance of their duty. This was followed by many baptisms and continual peace during the seventh year.

l: pride, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: In the eighth year, members of the church became proud because of their riches, fine clothing, flocks, herds, gold, silver, and other precious things. Their pride led them to scorn and persecute others and contributed to contentions and the church’s decline.

l: inequality, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma saw great inequality among the people. Some lifted themselves up in pride and despised and neglected the needy, while others abased themselves and gave substance and aid to those in need.

l: persecution, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Members of the church began to persecute those who did not believe according to their will and pleasure. Humble followers of God also suffered persecutions from the remainder of the people.

l: wickedness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: The wickedness of the church became a stumbling-block to those outside the church. Alma saw that its example led unbelievers from one piece of iniquity to another, and the church began to fail in its progress.

l: contentions among the people of the church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Great contentions arose among the people of the church in the eighth year. They included envyings, strife, malice, persecutions, and pride exceeding that of those outside the church.

l: destruction of the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma saw that the church’s example was leading unbelievers from one piece of iniquity to another, thus bringing on the destruction of the people.

l: appointment of Nephihah as chief judge, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma selected Nephihah, a wise man among the elders of the church, and gave him power according to the voice of the people. Nephihah was appointed chief judge to enact and enforce laws and to judge and govern the people.

l: Alma's relinquishment of the judgment-seat, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: At the commencement of the ninth year, Alma delivered the judgment-seat to Nephihah. Alma did not relinquish the high priesthood, which he retained for himself.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 4
s: Alma devoted himself to preaching the word of God among the people of Nephi and stirring them up in remembrance of their duty. He sought to reclaim them by bearing down in pure testimony against their pride, craftiness, and contentions.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Alma delivers the word of God to the people in Zarahemla and throughout the land, calling them to remember how God delivered their fathers and changed their hearts. He teaches that faith in Jesus Christ, repentance, and works of righteousness are necessary for salvation and preparation to meet God. Alma warns the people against pride, envy, persecution, riches, neglecting the poor, and following the devil, while inviting them to follow the good shepherd. He testifies by the Holy Spirit of God that Jesus Christ will come to take away the sins of those who steadfastly believe on his name.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Alma delivers the word of God to the people and teaches that they must repent, be born again, and bring forth works of righteousness. He testifies that Jesus Christ will come and that these things have been made known to him by the Holy Spirit of God.

l: Alma (father of Alma), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Alma's father was consecrated as a high priest over the church of God and established a church in the land of Mormon. He believed the words delivered by Abinadi, experienced a mighty change in his heart, and preached the word to his fathers.

l: Abinadi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Abinadi delivered words that Alma's father believed. He is identified as the source of words concerning Jesus Christ and the redemption of the people.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Jesus Christ is the Son, the Only Begotten of the Father, full of grace, mercy, and truth. He will come to take away the sins of every person who steadfastly believes on his name.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: God delivers people from bondage, changes hearts, and makes truth known by the Holy Spirit of God. God will judge people according to their deeds and will receive those who repent and bring forth works of righteousness.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The Holy Spirit of God makes truth known to Alma and manifests that the words spoken by the fathers are true. It is the source of the spirit of revelation and prophecy described by Alma.

l: church of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The church of God was established in the land of Mormon and throughout the land. Alma speaks by command to those who belong to the church and calls them to remain faithful, humble, and watchful.

l: children of men, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The people are taught to remember the captivity and deliverance of their fathers and are asked whether they have experienced a mighty change in their hearts. They are invited to repent, be baptized, follow the good shepherd, and prepare to meet God.

l: Alma's fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Alma's fathers were delivered from the hands of the people of king Noah, brought into bondage by the Lamanites, and delivered again by the power of God's word. They humbled themselves, trusted in God, were faithful until the end, and were saved.

l: people of king Noah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The people of king Noah held Alma's fathers in their hands before Alma's fathers were delivered by the mercy and power of God.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The Lamanites brought Alma's fathers into bondage in the wilderness. Alma's fathers were later delivered from that bondage by the power of God's word.

l: the wicked, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The wicked are those who persist in iniquity, pride, envy, persecution, costly apparel, riches, and turning their backs on the poor and needy. Their names will not be numbered among the righteous, and they will be hewn down and cast into the fire unless they repent.

l: the righteous, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The righteous are those whose garments are cleansed and spotless and who bring forth works meet for repentance. Their names will be written in the book of life, and they will receive an inheritance at God's right hand.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The devil is the shepherd of those who will not hearken to the voice of the good shepherd. Those who follow the devil bring forth evil works and receive death as their wages.

l: the good shepherd's sheep, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The good shepherd's sheep hearken to his voice and follow him. The good shepherd calls them into his fold and commands that no ravenous wolf be allowed to enter among them.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Zarahemla is the city where a church was established and where Alma delivers these words to the people.

l: land of Mormon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The land of Mormon was within the borders of Nephi, and Alma's father established a church there and baptized his brethren in its waters.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The kingdom of heaven is soon at hand, and those who do not repent cannot inherit it. Those who are not prepared to meet God do not have eternal life.

l: hell, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Hell encircled Alma's fathers with chains, but their chains were loosed through faith and a mighty change in their hearts.

l: tree of life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Those who come to God and repent may partake of the fruit of the tree of life.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The word of God delivers people from bondage and illuminates souls that are in darkness. Alma delivers it to the people and says that it must be fulfilled.

l: gospel invitation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The gospel invitation is extended to all men through the call to repent and come to God. Those who come may freely partake of the bread and waters of life and bring forth works of righteousness.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Repentance is required for people to be received by God, inherit the kingdom of heaven, and avoid being hewn down and cast into the fire. Alma repeatedly calls the people to repent quickly.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Faith in the words delivered by Abinadi led Alma's father to a mighty change in his heart. Steadfast belief in the name of Jesus Christ is connected with having sins taken away.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Salvation comes to those who believe, humble themselves, trust in the true and living God, and remain faithful until the end. No person can be saved while yielding themselves to become subjects to the devil.

l: mighty change of heart, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: A mighty change of heart was wrought in Alma's father and in his fathers after they believed, humbled themselves, and trusted in God. Alma asks whether the people have experienced this change and whether they can still feel to sing the song of redeeming love.

l: baptism, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Alma's father baptized his brethren in the waters of Mormon. Alma invites those who do not belong to the church to be baptized unto repentance so they may partake of the fruit of the tree of life.

l: judgment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: People will stand before God to be judged according to the deeds done in the mortal body. They are asked whether they can look up to God with a pure heart, clean hands, and God's image engraven upon their countenances.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Alma asks whether people look forward with an eye of faith to the mortal body being raised in immortality and corruption being raised in incorruption. This raising occurs before people stand before God to be judged.

l: death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The people were encircled by the bands of death, but those bands were broken and loosed through God's power. Those who follow the devil receive death as their wages concerning righteousness and are dead unto all good works.

l: blood of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: The blood of Christ cleanses garments from every stain. Alma teaches that garments must be purified through this blood for a person to be saved.

l: garments, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Garments must be washed white and cleansed from all stain. Alma asks whether the people have had their garments cleansed and made white through the blood of Christ.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Jesus Christ will come to take away the sins of those who steadfastly believe on his name. People who persist in sin and wickedness cannot be saved unless they repent.

l: pride, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 5
s: Alma warns that people must be stripped of pride to be prepared to meet God. Those who are puffed up in pride and set their hearts on the vain things of the world must repent.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: Alma ordained priests and elders to preside over and watch over the church in the city of Zarahemla. Those outside the church who repented were baptized and received, while members who refused to repent and humbled themselves were rejected and had their names blotted out. The children of God were commanded to gather often, fast, and pray for those who did not know God. Alma then went to the valley of Gideon and declared the word of God to the church there, testifying of Jesus Christ, the Son of God, who should come to redeem his people from their sins.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: Alma ordained priests and elders by laying on his hands to preside and watch over the church in the city of Zarahemla. After making regulations, he departed from Zarahemla and went to the valley of Gideon, where he declared the word of God to the church.

l: church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: The church in the city of Zarahemla received those outside it who repented and were baptized. Members who did not repent of their wickedness and humble themselves before God were rejected and had their names blotted out.

l: city of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: The city of Zarahemla had an established church over which priests and elders were appointed to preside and watch. Alma later departed from the city and went over the east side of the river Sidon to the valley of Gideon.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: God was the source of the order according to which Alma ordained priests and elders. The children of God were commanded to gather often, fast, and pray for the welfare of the souls of those who did not know God.

l: the valley of Gideon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: The valley of Gideon contained a city called the city of Gideon. Alma went there and declared the word of God to the church established in the valley.

l: the city of Gideon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: The city of Gideon had been built in the valley of Gideon and was named after the man who was slain by the hand of Nehor with the sword.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Son of God who should come to redeem his people from their sins. Alma declared the word of God according to the testimony of Jesus Christ.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 6
s: The word of God was liberal unto all, so that none were deprived of the privilege of assembling to hear it. Alma declared it to the church in the valley of Gideon according to the revelation of its truth.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The speaker comes to address the beloved brethren and urges them to repent, be baptized, keep God’s commandments, and walk in righteousness. The speaker testifies that the Son of God will come to earth, be born of Mary at Jerusalem, suffer for the pains and sins of his people, and overcome death. The speaker perceives that the beloved brethren have faith and are walking in the paths leading to the kingdom of God. The speaker exhorts them to be humble, patient, diligent, thankful, and full of faith, hope, and charity so they may enter the kingdom of heaven.

l: Helaman's father, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The speaker addresses the beloved brethren, testifies of the Son of God, and calls them to repentance, baptism, faith, and obedience. The speaker rejoices in their faith and righteousness and blesses them and their possessions.

l: beloved brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The beloved brethren are urged to humble themselves, repent, be baptized, keep the commandments, and walk blamelessly before God. The speaker perceives that they believe, have strong faith, and are in the paths of righteousness.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: Zarahemla is the place where the brethren had previously been in an awful dilemma.

l: brethren at Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The brethren at Zarahemla experienced much affliction and sorrow but were established again in the way of righteousness.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: God grants the speaker knowledge and joy concerning the brethren, has power to do all things according to his word, and receives worship, repentance, gratitude, and covenants. God does not dwell in unholy temples and does not vary from what he has said.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The Lord permits the speaker to come to the beloved brethren and grants that the speaker may address them. The people are commanded to prepare the way of the Lord and walk in his straight paths.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The Spirit testifies to the speaker that the Son of God will come upon the face of the earth and that the people must repent and be born again. The Spirit manifests the faith of the beloved brethren and testifies in the speaker.

l: Redeemer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The Redeemer is said to live and to come among his people, though the speaker does not know whether this will occur during his mortal dwelling.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The kingdom of heaven is at hand, and those who are not born again cannot inherit it. The righteous may enter it with spotless garments and remain there.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The Son of God will come upon the face of the earth, be born of Mary at Jerusalem, and suffer pains, afflictions, temptations, death, and the sins of his people. He will take upon himself their infirmities and provide deliverance.

l: Mary, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: Mary is described as a virgin and a precious, chosen vessel who will conceive by the power of the Holy Ghost and bring forth the Son of God.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: Jerusalem is identified as the land of the forefathers and as the place where Mary will bear the Son of God.

l: Holy Ghost, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The Holy Ghost will overshadow Mary, enabling her to conceive and bring forth a son, even the Son of God.

l: death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: Death binds the people, but the Son of God will take upon himself death so that he may loose its bands.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The people are commanded to repent and lay aside every sin. The Son of God will take upon himself the sins of his people and blot out their transgressions through his deliverance.

l: Lamb of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The Lamb of God takes away the sins of the world and is mighty to save and cleanse from all unrighteousness.

l: baptism, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: Baptism unto repentance is commanded so that people may be washed from their sins and show God their willingness to repent and enter into a covenant to keep his commandments.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: Repentance is required for people to be born again, receive cleansing, and inherit the kingdom of heaven. Those who repent are to witness their covenant by going into the waters of baptism.

l: eternal life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: Those who keep the commandments of God from the time of their covenant will have eternal life according to the testimony of the Holy Spirit.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The paths of righteousness lead to the kingdom of God, and the beloved brethren are perceived to be making his paths straight. Filthiness cannot be received into the kingdom of God.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The people are to have everlasting faith for the remission of their sins and to show faith in the Lamb of God. Their strong faith in the speaker’s teachings brings him great joy.

l: hope, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The beloved brethren are instructed to have hope along with faith and charity, after which they will always abound in good works.

l: charity, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 7
s: The beloved brethren are instructed to have charity together with faith and hope so that they will always abound in good works.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Alma teaches in Melek, is rejected and expelled from Ammonihah, and is commanded by an angel of the Lord to return and warn the people to repent or be destroyed. He returns, is fed by Amulek, and stays with him before beginning to preach again. Alma and Amulek preach to the people of Ammonihah with the power of the Holy Ghost, and they cannot be confined or slain until they are bound and imprisoned. The people of Ammonihah grow more wicked and seek to destroy the liberty of the people of Nephi.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Alma teaches in Gideon, Melek, and Ammonihah. After being rejected and expelled from Ammonihah, he returns at the command of an angel of the Lord, receives food from Amulek, and preaches with him to the people.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Amulek receives Alma into his house, gives him bread and meat, and is blessed by Alma. He later preaches with Alma to the people of Ammonihah with the power of the Holy Ghost.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: God calls Alma to teach according to his holy order and sends an angel of the Lord to command Alma to return to Ammonihah. God gives Alma and Amulek the spirit and power to preach, and their power is shown when they cannot be confined or slain.

l: angel of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: The angel of the Lord appears to Alma while he is weighed down with sorrow. The angel blesses him, reminds him that he delivered Alma's first message, and commands him to return to Ammonihah and warn the people to repent or be destroyed.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: The people of Nephi are ruled by judges. The people of Ammonihah study to destroy their liberty, contrary to the statutes, judgments, and commandments given to the people of Nephi.

l: the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: The people of Ammonihah reject Alma's preaching, revile him, spit upon him, and cast him out. They grow more wicked, study to destroy the liberty of the people of Nephi, and are warned to repent or face the Lord's anger and destruction.

l: church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Alma establishes the order of the church in Gideon and had previously done so in Zarahemla. The people of Ammonihah say they are not of Alma's church and do not believe in its traditions.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Ammonihah is a city named after the man who first possessed the land. Alma preaches there, is expelled, returns by another way, and later preaches there with Amulek.

l: preaching, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Alma begins preaching the word of God in Ammonihah, but the people will not hearken. After being commanded by an angel of the Lord to return, he preaches again with Amulek and declares the words of God.

l: Alma's rejection and expulsion from Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: The people of Ammonihah withstand Alma's words, revile him, spit upon him, and cause him to be cast out of the city. Alma departs toward Aaron in sorrow before the angel of the Lord commands him to return.

l: the angel's message to Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: The angel's message tells Alma to lift up his head and rejoice because he has been faithful. It commands him to return to Ammonihah, preach again, and warn that the Lord God will destroy the people unless they repent.

l: Amulek's feeding Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Amulek recognizes Alma as a holy prophet of God and takes him into his house. He gives Alma bread and meat after Alma has fasted many days.

l: Alma and Amulek's preaching, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Alma and Amulek go among the people of Ammonihah to declare the words of God and prophesy. They are filled with the Holy Ghost and receive power so they cannot be confined in dungeons or slain, until they are bound and cast into prison.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: Alma and Amulek preach that the people of Ammonihah must repent. The Lord warns that unless they repent, he will visit them in anger and will not turn away his fierce anger.

l: destruction of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 8
s: The angel of the Lord tells Alma to warn the people of Ammonihah that the Lord God will destroy them unless they repent. The text records the warning, not the destruction itself.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Alma and Amulek preach repentance to the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, who challenge Alma and become angry at his testimony. Alma reminds them of God’s commandments, the deliverance and blessings given to the people of Nephi, and the consequences of continuing in wickedness. He declares that the Son of God will soon come, redeem those baptized unto repentance, and judge all people according to their works. Amulek then begins preaching to them, though only part of his words is recorded.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Alma is commanded by God to take Amulek and preach again to the people who were in the city of Ammonihah. He boldly testifies of their wickedness, calls them to repentance, warns them of destruction, and is opposed when they seek to seize him.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Amulek accompanies Alma in preaching to the people who were in the city of Ammonihah. After Alma speaks, Amulek stands forth and begins to preach, though only part of his words is recorded.

l: the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The people contend with Alma, question his authority, and refuse to believe his words. They are described as hard-hearted, stiffnecked, lost, and fallen; they become angry and seek to cast Alma into prison.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Ammonihah is the city whose people hear Alma and Amulek preach. Its destruction is presented as a possible consequence if its people refuse to repent.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: God commands Alma to preach, has delivered and preserved the people of Nephi, and gives commandments concerning prosperity and being cut off from his presence. God is described as merciful to those who call on his name and as unwilling to allow people to live in iniquity.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The Lamanites have been cut off from the presence of the Lord because of their transgressions, but promises are extended to them because of the traditions of their fathers. They will eventually be brought to believe in God’s word, and they may be sent upon the people of Ammonihah if those people do not repent.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The people of Nephi have received great light, knowledge, blessings, deliverance, spiritual gifts, and prosperity from the Lord. Because of these blessings, transgression would be less tolerable for them than for the Lamanites, and rebellion could result in their destruction.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Son of God who will come in glory, full of grace, equity, truth, patience, mercy, and long-suffering. He will redeem those who are baptized unto repentance through faith on his name and will provide salvation according to his power and deliverance.

l: angel of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The angel has visited many of God’s people and declared that they must cry mightily to the people of Ammonihah to repent because the kingdom of heaven is near.

l: people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The people of Ammonihah are called a hard-hearted and stiffnecked people because they have forgotten the traditions of their fathers and the commandments of God. They become angry when Alma uses this description.

l: the land, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The land is promised to prosper those who keep God’s commandments. Those who refuse to keep them may be cut off from the presence of the Lord and destroyed from the face of the earth.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The kingdom of God cannot be inherited by those who refuse to repent.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The commandments of God are presented as something the people of Ammonihah have forgotten. Keeping them brings prosperity in the land, while refusing them leads to being cut off from the presence of the Lord.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The word of God has caused many people to be visited by an angel and commanded to preach repentance. The people of Ammonihah have hardened their hearts against it.

l: the tradition of the Lamanites' fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The people of Ammonihah have forgotten the traditions of their fathers, while the traditions of the Lamanites have contributed to their ignorance. The Lamanites will eventually learn that those traditions are incorrect.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Repentance is commanded as necessary to inherit the kingdom of God and avoid destruction. People who are baptized unto repentance through faith in Jesus Christ can be redeemed.

l: destruction of the people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The destruction of Ammonihah is presented as a possible future event if its people continue in wickedness. The people do not believe that the great city could be destroyed in one day.

l: judgment day, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The day of judgment will be more tolerable for the Lamanites than for the people of Ammonihah if the latter remain in their sins.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The coming of Jesus Christ is declared to be near, with the Son of God expected to come in glory not many days after the preaching described in this unit.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Salvation of the soul is promised to those who are righteous, according to the power and deliverance of Jesus Christ.

l: damnation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Damnation of the soul is the result awaiting those who are evil, according to the power and captivation of the devil.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: The devil is associated with the power and captivation according to which evil people will reap the damnation of their souls.

l: preaching, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 9
s: Preaching is commanded by God and carried out by Alma and Amulek among the people who were in the city of Ammonihah. Its message includes repentance, the coming of Jesus Christ, and the consequences of righteousness and wickedness.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: Amulek recounts how an angel of the Lord sent him home to feed Alma, a holy prophet, and how Alma’s presence blessed his household. He testifies that Alma’s teachings are true and warns the people of Ammonihah that their wickedness, lawyers, and judges are laying the foundation for destruction. The people and lawyers oppose Amulek, while Zeezrom becomes the foremost accuser of Amulek and Alma. Amulek declares that the prayers of the righteous are sparing the people from famine, pestilence, and the sword.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: Amulek identifies himself as the son of Giddonah and a descendant of Nephi and Manasseh. He recounts his former rebellion, his encounter with an angel, his reception of Alma, and his testimony against the wickedness of the people, lawyers, and judges.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: Alma is described as a holy, chosen man of God who had fasted many days because of the sins of the people. He stayed at Amulek’s house, where his presence was associated with blessings, and he testified with Amulek.

l: Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: Zeezrom is one of the lawyers and is foremost in accusing Amulek and Alma. He is described as one of the most expert lawyers, with much business among the people.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: God is the source of the marvelous power and mysteries witnessed by Amulek. Amulek says the lawyers are laying the foundation of the devil and bringing God’s wrath upon themselves and the people.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The Lord sends an angel to Amulek, blesses Amulek’s household, and calls the people to repent. Amulek says the Lord may bring famine, pestilence, and the sword upon them if they cast out the righteous.

l: angel of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The angel of the Lord appears to Amulek while he is journeying and commands him to return home, receive Alma, and feed him. The angel says Alma is a holy and chosen man of God and promises blessings upon Amulek and his house.

l: the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The people of Ammonihah hear the testimonies of Amulek and Alma, but many become angry and accuse Amulek of reviling their laws and lawyers. They are warned that their transgression makes them ripe for destruction unless they repent.

l: the righteous, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The righteous people in the land are preserving the people from immediate destruction through their prayers. Amulek warns that casting them out would remove this protection.

l: lawyers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The lawyers are hired or appointed to administer the law and are learned in the arts and cunning of the people. They seek to trap Amulek and Alma, pervert the ways of the righteous, and gain wealth through their profession.

l: judges, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The judges are selected to judge crimes under the law. Amulek says the unrighteousness of the lawyers and judges is beginning to lay the foundation of the people’s destruction.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The land of Ammonihah is where Amulek preaches to the people. It contains people whose sins and rejection of the righteous place them under warning of famine, pestilence, the sword, and destruction.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The kingdom of heaven is declared to be at hand as the Lord calls the people to repent.

l: law, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The people claim that Amulek reviles their just laws, but Amulek says he has spoken in favor of the law to their condemnation. He distinguishes opposition to their unrighteousness from opposition to the law itself.

l: prayers of the righteous, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The prayers of the righteous are the reason the people have been spared from utter destruction. Amulek says that without those prayers, destruction would come by famine, pestilence, and the sword.

l: destruction of the people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The people are described as becoming ripe for destruction when their voice chooses iniquity and they fall into transgression. Their destruction is being laid as a foundation by the unrighteousness of their lawyers and judges, but repentance could prevent it.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: Alma has fasted because of the sins of the people. Amulek warns that the people’s sins and transgressions have brought them under the Lord’s judgment.

l: angel's commission to Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The angel’s commission to Amulek is to return home, receive Alma, feed him, and accept the blessing promised to his household. Amulek obeys and finds Alma as instructed.

l: Amulek's testimony, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: Amulek testifies that Alma is a holy man and that Alma’s teachings are true because an angel of God made these things manifest to him. He also testifies that Alma’s presence brought blessings to his household and kindred.

l: questioning of Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 10
s: The lawyers begin questioning Amulek in order to make him contradict himself and create evidence against him. Amulek perceives their designs and condemns their attempts to trap the holy ones of God.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: The unit explains the law of Mosiah concerning judges’ wages, monetary reckoning, debt enforcement, and the motives of those who stirred up disturbances for gain. Zeezrom questions Amulek and offers him six onties of silver to deny the existence of a Supreme Being, but Amulek affirms that there is one true and living God. Amulek teaches that the Son of God will come to redeem those who believe, will not save people in their sins, and is the Eternal Father of heaven and earth. He further teaches that all people will be resurrected, restored, and judged before God according to their works.

l: law of Mosiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: The law of Mosiah required judges to receive wages according to the time they labored and established the reckoning and measures used by the Nephites.

l: judges, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Judges received wages for their service, enforced payment of debts, and judged people according to the law and the evidence brought against them. Some stirred up riots and disturbances to increase the number of cases and their earnings.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Alma was opposed by those who stirred up the people for the purpose of gaining more employment and money through legal suits.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Amulek refused Zeezrom’s offer to deny the existence of a Supreme Being. He testified that there is one true and living God, that the Son of God will come to redeem believers, and that all people will be resurrected and judged according to their works.

l: Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Zeezrom questioned Amulek and offered him six onties of silver if he would deny the existence of a Supreme Being. He was described as expert in the devices of the devil, and he later trembled after hearing Amulek’s words.

l: Supreme Being, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: The existence of a Supreme Being was challenged by Zeezrom, but Amulek affirmed it.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Amulek testified that there is one true and living God. He taught that people will stand before God and be judged according to their works.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: The Son of God will come into the world to redeem his people, but he will not save them in their sins. Amulek identified him as the very Eternal Father of heaven and earth and said that he will judge the resurrected.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Salvation comes to those who believe on the name of the Son of God and to none else. People cannot be saved in their sins because no unclean thing can inherit the kingdom of heaven.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: No unclean thing can inherit the kingdom of heaven, so people cannot be saved in their sins.

l: redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: The redemption made by the Son of God benefits those who believe on his name, while the wicked remain as though there had been no redemption made except for the loosing of the bands of death.

l: temporal death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Temporal death is a death from which all people will be raised. The spirit and body will be reunited in a perfect and immortal form.

l: death of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: The death of Christ will loose the bands of temporal death so that all people will be raised from temporal death.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: All people will rise from the dead, with their spirits and bodies reunited in perfect form. Their bodies will become immortal and will no longer see corruption.

l: judgment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: After the resurrection, all people will stand before God and be judged according to their works, whether good or evil.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 11
s: Christ is identified as the Son of God and the Eternal Father of heaven and earth. He will preside at the judgment of all people after their resurrection.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Alma explains to Zeezrom and the people that Zeezrom lied to men and God under the influence of the devil, and that hardened hearts receive less of the word and become subject to destruction. He teaches that death, resurrection, judgment, spiritual death, and the consequences of sin are part of God's plan, while repentance and faith in the Only Begotten Son bring mercy and entry into God's rest. Alma explains to Antionah that Adam's Fall made mankind fallen, established a probationary state, and made the plan of redemption necessary. He urges the people to repent, harden not their hearts, and avoid provoking God's wrath.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Alma speaks to Zeezrom and the people, establishes Amulek's words, and explains the scriptures concerning the plan of redemption, death, resurrection, judgment, repentance, and God's rest. He teaches that hardened hearts receive a lesser portion of the word and urges the people to repent.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Amulek's words silence Zeezrom, and Alma establishes and expands upon them. He had spoken concerning death, resurrection, and being brought before the bar of God to be judged according to works.

l: Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Zeezrom is exposed as having lied to men and God and as having used a subtle plan to deceive the people. He trembles under a consciousness of his guilt, becomes convinced of God's power, and asks Alma about the kingdom of God and the resurrection of the dead.

l: Adam, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Adam fell by partaking of the forbidden fruit, and through his fall all mankind became a lost and fallen people. If he had partaken of the tree of life then, there would have been no death and God's word would have been void.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: God knows all thoughts, gives commandments, appoints death and judgment, and sends angels to make His glory and the plan of redemption known. He is just in all His works, merciful to mankind, and has power to save those who believe in His name and bring forth fruit meet for repentance.

l: Satan, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Satan has power to subject people according to his will and to chain them down to everlasting destruction. Those who harden their hearts and die in their sins are described as being under his power and captivity.

l: devil, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The devil influences Zeezrom's subtle plan to lie and deceive the people. Those who harden their hearts receive less of the word until they know nothing of God's mysteries and are taken captive by the devil.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Through the Only Begotten Son, those who repent and harden not their hearts can claim mercy unto a remission of their sins. God calls on men in the name of His Son as part of the plan of redemption.

l: children of men, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The people hear Alma's words, become more astonished, and are warned that the adversary seeks to bring them into subjection and destruction. They are urged to repent, harden not their hearts, and enter into the rest of God.

l: our first parents, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The first parents could not partake of the tree of life after the Fall, because doing so would have left them forever miserable without a preparatory state. Their condition relates to the need for the plan of redemption and the appointment of death and judgment.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Zeezrom asks Alma to know more concerning the kingdom of God. Alma's explanation connects knowledge of God's mysteries with the heed and diligence people give to Him.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The resurrection of the dead will bring all people, both just and unjust, to stand before God and be judged according to their works. It is brought to pass through the plan of redemption.

l: judgment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: After death, people must come to judgment and stand before God to acknowledge that His judgments are just. Judgment is according to their works, words, and thoughts.

l: temporal death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Temporal death is the death that comes upon mankind and involves being raised from mortality to an immortal state. This life was granted as a time to prepare to meet God before the resurrection and judgment.

l: second death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Spiritual death is a second death concerning things pertaining to righteousness. Those who die in their sins as to temporal death also die spiritually and face everlasting destruction.

l: immortality, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: After being raised from mortality, people are brought to an immortal state in which the soul can never die. Immortality is discussed in connection with the resurrection and judgment.

l: redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The plan of redemption was laid from the foundation of the world and brings to pass the resurrection of the dead. It provides a way for repentant people to receive mercy through the Only Begotten Son, while it has no power to destroy the works of justice for those who do iniquity.

l: the probationary state, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: This life became a probationary state after death came upon mankind. It is a time to repent and prepare to meet God and for the endless state after the resurrection.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Repentance is required to avoid condemnation and enter into the rest of God. Those who repent and harden not their hearts receive mercy through the Only Begotten Son and a remission of their sins.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Those who die in their sins die a spiritual death and cannot be redeemed according to God's justice. Sin and iniquity bring condemnation and provoke God's wrath.

l: righteousness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Spiritual death is death as to things pertaining to righteousness. Those who do not repent face everlasting death and destruction concerning righteousness.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Mercy is available through the Only Begotten Son to whoever repents and hardens not their heart. Through mercy, repentant people may receive a remission of their sins and enter God's rest.

l: justice, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: God's judgments and works are just, and justice condemns those whose hearts, words, works, and thoughts are not spotless. The plan of redemption cannot destroy the works of justice.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Those who harden their hearts against the word receive a lesser portion until they know nothing concerning God's mysteries. God's word appoints death, judgment, and the consequences of iniquity, and it will not be void.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: God gives commandments after making the plan of redemption known. The commandments prohibit evil and carry the penalty of a second, everlasting death for those who do iniquity.

l: tree of life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The tree of life could not be partaken of by the first parents after the Fall, because doing so would have prevented death and the preparatory state. Partaking of it then would have frustrated the plan of redemption.

l: garden of Eden, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: God placed cherubim and a flaming sword on the east of the garden of Eden to prevent the first parents from entering and partaking of the tree of life and living forever.

l: chains of hell, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The chains of hell describe the condition of those who harden their hearts, lose knowledge of God's mysteries, and are taken captive by the devil and led to destruction.

l: lake of fire and brimstone, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: The torments of those who die spiritually are described as being like a lake of fire and brimstone whose flame ascends forever and ever.

l: hell, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Hell is associated with chains that bind people who harden their hearts and are taken captive by the devil. These chains lead them down to destruction.

l: everlasting destruction, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 12
s: Everlasting destruction is the fate of those chained down by Satan's power and captivity or condemned through unrepented iniquity. It is connected with spiritual death and the inability of justice to be destroyed.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Alma teaches that the Lord God ordained priests and high priests after the holy order of the Only Begotten Son to teach the commandments and help the people look forward to redemption. He explains that holy calling and high priesthood are prepared for those who choose good, exercise faith, repent, and work righteousness, while many are sanctified and enter into the rest of the Lord. Alma recounts that Melchizedek preached repentance in the land of Salem, and the people repented and received peace. He urges the people to repent without delay, humble themselves, pray continually, and prepare for the coming of the Son, which angels declare with glad tidings.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The Lord God gave commandments to his children and ordained priests after the holy order of the Only Begotten Son to teach them.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Alma teaches about the holy order, high priesthood, faith, repentance, and the rest of the Lord. He urges the people to repent, humble themselves, pray continually, and not procrastinate the day of their repentance.

l: Melchizedek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Melchizedek was a high priest after the holy order and a king over the land of Salem. He preached repentance to his wicked people, who repented, and he established peace, becoming known as the prince of peace.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The Only Begotten Son is the one after whose order priests and high priests are ordained. He was prepared as part of the atonement and redemption, and his coming is declared by angels.

l: angels, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Angels declare the voice of the Lord and glad tidings of great joy to all nations and peoples. They prepare the hearts of the children of men for the coming of the Son and will declare it to just and holy men at that time.

l: priests, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Priests were ordained by the Lord God after the holy order of the Only Begotten Son to teach the commandments to the people and help them look forward to redemption.

l: high priests, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: High priests are called and ordained to the high priesthood of the holy order of God to teach the commandments so that people may enter into the rest of the Lord. They are sanctified through faith, repentance, and righteousness, and their garments are washed white through the blood of the Lamb.

l: the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The people are taught to look forward to the Son for a remission of their sins and to enter into the rest of the Lord. Alma calls on them to humble themselves, bring forth fruit meet for repentance, and cast off their sins.

l: children of men, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The children of men are taught the commandments and are prepared to receive the word of the Son at the time of his coming in glory. They are urged to repent, pray, and be led by the Holy Spirit.

l: land of Salem, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The land of Salem was ruled by Melchizedek when its people had become full of wickedness and abomination. Peace was established in the land after the people repented.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The commandments were given by the Lord God and are taught by priests and high priests after the holy order of the Son.

l: holy order of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The holy order is the order of the Son and has existed from the foundation of the world, without beginning of days or end of years. Priests and high priests are ordained after this order to teach and lead people toward redemption and the rest of the Lord.

l: high priesthood of the holy order of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The high priesthood of the holy order of God is received through a holy calling and holy ordinance. It is after the order of the Son and is without beginning or end.

l: holy calling, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The holy calling was prepared from the foundation of the world according to the foreknowledge of God for those who choose good, exercise faith, and do good works. Those who receive it are ordained to the high priesthood of the holy order.

l: redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: A preparatory redemption made the holy calling possible for those who were called according to faith. The people are taught to look forward to the Son for redemption.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The atonement of the Only Begotten Son is connected with the holy calling prepared from the foundation of the world.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Exceeding faith is associated with being called to the holy calling and becoming a high priest. Melchizedek exercised mighty faith before preaching repentance, and people are urged to have faith on the Lord.

l: sin, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Those who are sanctified and made pure cannot look upon sin except with abhorrence. Alma urges the people to cast off their sins and repent.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Repentance is required for people to bring forth fruit, receive sanctification, and enter into the rest of the Lord. Alma urges the people not to delay repentance, and Melchizedek preached repentance to his people, who repented.
